topics.topic: Choose the digest representation and comparison method for expected file outputs
questions: Must authored expected file outputs store the hexadecimal SHA-256 used for sandbox file outputs, or must execute_trial_case compare files using content_identity of BytesContent instead?
Must expected file outputs store the hexadecimal SHA-256 of their bytes as value_digest, or must execute_trial_case compare their content_identity(BytesContent) digests instead?

quotes: - add_trial_case: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] Each input value becomes a StoredValue with the stored schema of its port (M21: the port's value_schema, or for a many port the canonical array schema with it as items) and the class its contract input port declares, each expected output a StoredValue with its port's stored schema and the highest class of the case's inputs from highest_disclosure_class; value_digest is content_identity of a BytesContent holding the bytes, value_id content_identity of the StoredValueContent, and the bytes are stored with put_value_bytes; a port refers to its values by StoredValuesRef entries naming it: one StoredValuesRef for a value port, and for a many file port one StoredValuesRef per file, consecutive in list order; inputs and expected_outputs MUST list these refs in port name order by Unicode code point, so that equal facts give an equal TrialCaseContent.

- execute_trial_case: [BEHAVIOR] The outcome is the sandbox outcome of the same name; a succeeded execution is passed when the case has no expected outputs or every output's digest equals the expected one — a value output's digest is content_identity of a BytesContent holding its canonical bytes and a file output's is the hexadecimal SHA-256 of the bytes of its FilePayload content, or of each FileListPayload contents item in list order, the content_digest its FileFacts records, both computed from what the sandbox returned, and an expected output's is read from its stored record; the outcome is decided before any output is written, so no output is read back from the store —, a many file output equal only with the same length and equal digests position by position, and output_mismatch otherwise; a succeeded value output whose canonical bytes exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant makes the outcome contract_violation.
judgement.why: Authored expected file outputs are assigned content_identity(BytesContent) digests, while sandbox file outputs are assigned hexadecimal SHA-256 digests and compared directly against those stored expected digests.

topics.topic: Whether answer_request JSON-text size bounds are measured before or after canonicalization
questions: Must JSON-text request bounds be measured using canonical_bytes, or from the UTF-8 text as received with canonical_bytes first applied only after all request bounds pass?
Must answer_request measure each JSON text's bound using canonical_bytes and refuse an oversized canonical form, or measure the received UTF-8 text and allow its canonical form to exceed that bound?

judgement.why: This asks the same question as P1, and neither the relevant passages nor the change since that judgement altered the answer.

precedent.topic: Whether JSON-text bounds are measured on received UTF-8 text or canonical bytes
quotes: Request bounds, each counted as UTF-8 bytes of the field as received: implementation code within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_IMPLEMENTATION_CODE_BYTES_MAX constant; the json_text of a trial case input or expected output, of a flow constant and of a run input within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant; the decoded bytes of a trial case file within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_TRIAL_FIXTURE_BYTES_MAX constant; every other string anywhere in the request within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_BOUNDED_TEXT_BYTES_MAX constant; a page_size given below 1 or above the imported RELEASE_CEILING_PAGE_SIZE_MAX constant; base64 text that does not decode; each a failure answered invalid_request (A16 rules 4 and 6).

After every request bound is checked on the texts as received, as the last step of the fit check, before the actor check and before any handler runs, MUST replace every JSON text the request carries — the json_text of each RequestJsonValue and RequestConstant, the value_schema of every Port and RequestConstant, the guard_value of every EdgeGuard — by its canonical form obtained from canonical_bytes; a NonCanonicalValueError there is invalid_request, so modules below receive only canonical JSON (A01 rule 1). A text whose canonical form outgrows a bound it met as received is not refused here: the module that judges the value measures its canonical bytes, as start_run refuses a run input whose canonical bytes exceed the stored value ceiling.
precedent.why: The text explicitly requires request bounds to be measured on the UTF-8 bytes as received before canonicalization and explicitly permits the canonical form to outgrow such a bound.
